title: Propp — Dramatis Personae (Character Roles / Spheres of Action)
source: Vladimir Propp, Morphology of the Folktale (1928)
license: system/idea (not copyrightable); descriptions authored for monomyth
tier_note: Seven spheres of action. A single character may fill several roles, and one role may be split across several characters.

items.name: Villain
items.description: Struggles against the hero; causes the harm or lack that drives the tale.

items.name: Donor
items.description: Tests the hero and provides the magical agent or crucial knowledge.

items.name: Helper
items.description: Aids the hero: guides, rescues, solves tasks, and transfigures.

items.name: Princess
items.sphere: assignment of difficult tasks, branding, exposure, recognition, punishment, marriage
items.description: The sought-for person and their parent; sets tasks, recognizes and rewards the hero.

items.name: Dispatcher
items.description: Sends the hero off on the quest; makes the lack known.

items.name: Hero
items.sphere: departure on search, reaction to donor, wedding
items.description: The protagonist who departs, reacts to the donor, and ultimately weds/is rewarded. May be a seeker-hero or a victim-hero.

items.name: False Hero
items.sphere: departure on search, reaction to donor, unfounded claims
items.description: Claims the hero's achievements; presents false claims and is ultimately exposed.
